response.rationale: All 11 cited items are positive and none are negative. They include several T1 meta-analyses (Bisra 2018, Kobayashi 2019, Nesbit 2006, Alfieri 2013, Dunlosky 2013) and classroom and lab studies (Chi 1989 and 1994, Menekse 2013) that link elaborative activities such as self-explanation, teaching and concept mapping to higher learning and exam scores. Some items are repeated: the Chi 1989 and Dunlosky 2013 entries each appear twice, and the Chi 1994 entry has the same text as them. That makes the evidence count look larger than it is. Dunlosky rates elaborative interrogation and self-explanation only MODERATE, and several items are about causal manipulation of learning, not prediction of achievement. Even so, the direction is consistent.
